title: fix(components): a data-table save removes only what it sent, so an edit made during the save stays pending (objectui#12322)
body:
Fixes #12322
Clause-②: no

Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 1 (claim comment 6143490908). Implementing session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01CsyMRsFJBKNEMa4oPY1b5z`.

**Why `Clause-②: no`:** no published type, export, prop or accepted input moves. `onRowSave`, `onBatchSave` and the `{ failed }` outcome keep their shapes, and their `@object-ui/types` docblocks are not edited. Everything new (`removeSentEdits`, the `inFlight` argument of `stageCellChange`, `inFlightRef`, `whileInFlight`) is private to `data-table.tsx`. No new prop, spec key, export or i18n key.

## What changed

`@object-ui/components` `data-table` (`packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx`). Cell editing stays open while a row save or Save All is in flight. A save now settles against the pending edits as they stand when it returns, and removes only what it sent.

- **Settle from the current state.** `saveRow` and `saveBatch` settle with a `setPendingChanges` updater, `removeSentEdits(prev, sent)`. For each record the save sent, it removes each column whose pending value is still the very value sent (`Object.is`). The record's entry goes once nothing else is staged on it. On a per-row `{ failed }`, only the records that landed are passed, so a failed record keeps every edit.
- **A cell whose save is in flight is always staged.** While a save is on the wire, `inFlightRef` holds what it sent, per record. `stageCellChange` takes that record's entry and never calls a commit on one of those cells "unchanged", even when it equals the loaded value. The record will hold the sent value once the save lands, so the loaded value is a change again. The settle then decides what stays.
- **The settle closes only the editor that was open when the save was pressed.** An editor opened during the save stays open with what was typed. Before, Save All closed whatever editor was open at settle, and a row save closed the current editor whenever the press-time one had been on that row.
- **`saveEdit` stages through an updater**, as `stageEdit` already did. The same line now passes the in-flight entry.
- **A rejected Save All flags the records it sent** (`sent.keys()`). This is the same set as before, read from the sent map, so a record staged during the save is not flagged.
- **Docs:** a paragraph in `content/docs/components/complex/data-table.mdx` and a bullet in `packages/plugin-grid/README.md`.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/12322-save-removes-only-what-it-sent.md`, `@object-ui/components` `patch`.
- `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` is not touched. Its `defaultRowSave` / `defaultBatchSave` are the named producer, and nothing in them rebuilds the table's pending state.

## Rulings (triage 6143051525)

- **Compute the next pending map from the current pending state when the save settles:** both saves settle with the `removeSentEdits` updater. ⛔ No settle path reads the map captured before the `await`.
- **Remove exactly the entries sent, and only where the value is still the one sent:** per record and per column, by identity. See Zone 2 item 2.
- **A per-row `{ failed }` keeps the failed rows pending:** kept. It is pinned with a third record staged during the save, which stays pending and unflagged.
- **⛔ Cell editing is not disabled during a save:** nothing is disabled. `isSaving` still disables only the save and cancel buttons.
- **The three pins:** all present, in the components file below.

## Measured before writing (Zone 2)

1. **The mechanism, read at `b64fda3`.** It was as the claim says. `saveRow` built `new Map(pendingChanges)` after its `await`, from the render-time map. `saveBatch` set a filter of the captured map, or `new Map()`. The reject path flagged `pendingChanges.keys()` of the captured map.
   - **Red first, on the real `data-table` with the save promise held open, at `b64fda3`:** 8 of the 9 new components pins failed. Both of the card's sequences failed with `Unable to find an element with the text: /1 row modified/` after release: Bravo's edit was gone. The per-row `{ failed }` pin read no `/2 rows modified/`: Charlie's edit was gone. The re-edit pins lost Alpha's `12`.
   - **Two more paths the card did not name, both red at `b64fda3`.**
     - A cell re-edited back to its loaded value during its own save was un-staged at stage time, compared with the stale loaded value. The pin failed before release: no `/1 row modified/`. Once the save lands, the record holds the sent value, so that edit was lost.
     - An editor opened during Save All was closed by the settle, and a built-in editor's typed value went with it: `expected null not to be null` for Bravo's input after release.
   - The ninth pin, "a rejected Save All flags the rows it sent, not a row staged during the save", is green before and after. It guards the reject path against a settle-time reading, which would flag a record that was never sent.
2. **What "the same value" means: identity (`Object.is`), not `isUnchangedCellValue`.**
   - What the editors stage: a single lookup stages the picked option's `value`, a scalar id (`LookupField` calls `onChange(option.value)`). A multiple lookup and a multi-select stage a new array on every toggle. The number editor stages the input's string. So identity and value equality differ only for arrays and objects.
   - The settle asks whether the cell was staged again since it was sent. `stageCellChange` copies the row's other columns by reference, so a column nobody touched keeps the exact value sent, and identity answers yes. A value staged again during the save is kept, even an equal copy (a set toggled off and on again). That costs at most one redundant write. That is the safe direction `isUnchangedCellValue`'s own comment names. A looser equality would remove an edit.
   - `isUnchangedCellValue` answers a different question ("is this the loaded value, despite the editor's round trip?"), and it treats a number and its decimal string, and two sets in another order, as one value.
3. **`erroredRows` and `saveError`.** Neither needs a settle-time reading. Their only writers are the two saves and the two cancels. While a save is in flight, the cancels and the other save are disabled, so nothing else can write either during the round trip, and the replace forms in `saveBatch` overwrite nothing.
   - The one place where "current versus sent" matters is the reject path. It must flag what was sent, not what is pending now. It did, from the captured map, and now reads `sent.keys()` (pinned, see 1).
   - A record re-edited during a failed save stays pending with its new value and stays flagged. The flag says its last save attempt failed, which is true.
   - A record re-edited during a successful row save stays pending and loses its flag. Its last attempt succeeded.

## Beyond the triage's three sentences (declared)

- **The in-flight staging rule** is the ruling's own sentence, "An edit that changed again during the save stays pending with its new value", applied to the one new value the stage path used to drop: the loaded one.
- **The editor-close guard** is a bounded in-place repair. It is the same defect class (a settle acting on state it did not start with), a mechanical change of the same shape, in a file no other claim holds, inside the same gate family. Its evidence is the red pin above.
- **`saveEdit` as an updater** is unmeasured. Its window is a user commit between a save's settle and that settle's render. It rides the line this change already edits for the in-flight argument.

## Pins

- `packages/components/src/__tests__/data-table-save-settles-current-12322.test.tsx`: the real `data-table`, with the save promise held open by hand.
  - a row save held open: an edit staged on another row stays pending and drawn when it settles;
  - Save All held open: the same;
  - row save and Save All: the cell being saved, re-edited during the save, keeps its new value pending;
  - a cell re-edited back to its loaded value during its save stays pending;
  - another cell of the row being saved, staged during its save, stays pending on its own;
  - Save All with a per-row `{ failed }`: the failed row stays flagged, and a row staged during the save stays unflagged;
  - a rejected Save All flags the rows it sent, not a row staged during the save;
  - an editor opened during the save stays open, with what was typed, when the save settles.
  - Each pin then presses Save All and asserts what is handed over, so "pending" is read off the next write, not only the dirty bar.
- `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/inlineEditDuringSave-12322.test.tsx`: the console path end to end. It renders the real `ObjectGrid`, `data-table` and field-widget editors, and writes through the real `@object-ui/data-objectstack` adapter against a `fetch` stub that holds each write open. For a row save and for Save All: an estimate staged on another row is still pending after the save lands and the grid re-reads, and the next Save All writes it.

## Ablation (one leg: restore the captured-map settle)

Run with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (the `../objectstack` helper, from this worktree) on `data-table.tsx` at `80a7e35`. `data-table.tsx` is unchanged after that commit.

- **Mutation:** the anchor `setPendingChanges((prev) => removeSentEdits(prev, sent));` (×2: the row save's settle and Save All's full-success settle) is replaced by `setPendingChanges(removeSentEdits(pendingChanges, sent));`. That is the same removal, applied to the copy read when the save was pressed.
- **On disk:** anchor 2 → 0, replacement 0 → 2, blob `e30200ca773f` → `1d386008e93c`.
- **Run:** both pin files. They reach `data-table` through the vitest alias to `src`, so there is no build leg.
- **Result:** `Tests  8 failed | 3 passed (11)`, in the predicted direction.
  - Red: the six components pins that settle through those two lines, and both grid pins.
  - Green: the per-row `{ failed }` pin (its settle is the `landed` line, which was not mutated), the reject pin, and the editor pin.
- **Restore:** blob after restore == HEAD (`e30200ca773f`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Gates

The final commit is `b07e8ae`. Every full run below is cited from a run at that HEAD, and no commit follows it.

- **Dependency closure:** `turbo run build --concurrency=2 --filter=@object-ui/components^... --filter=@object-ui/plugin-grid^...` exits 0. Neither closure contains a file this diff touches.
- **`pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check`:** exits 0 at `b07e8ae`. The script echoes `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the test files are covered. The first run, at `80a7e35`, exited 2 on two type errors in the new components test file, and `b07e8ae` repairs them.
- **`pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid type-check`:** exits 0. Nothing in plugin-grid changed after that run.
- **Verify lock, `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/components/`:** `Test Files  381 passed | 1 skipped (382)`, `Tests  3865 passed | 24 skipped (3889)`, exit 0, at `b07e8ae`. The skipped file is a pre-existing time-zone `skipIf`.
- **Verify lock, `packages/plugin-grid/`:** `Test Files  210 passed (210)`, `Tests  1920 passed (1920)`, exit 0, at `b07e8ae`.
- **Verify lock, the other inline-edit suites, re-derived by grep** for suites that render a grid and name inline edit or Save All:
  - `packages/plugin-list/`;
  - plugin-view: `ObjectView.namedViewInlineEdit-10885`, `tableEditable-10976`, `namedViewEditInlineFold-5144`, `namedViewProtocolKeys-8980`, `routeTwoNamedGridMembers-10885`, `tableSlotRelay-10976`, `objectViewHostSurface`;
  - app-shell: `ObjectView.inlineEditSessionOnly-5144`, `InterfaceListPage.editInlineFold-5144`, `ObjectView.fallbackTabSessionOnly-11643`, `viewDescriptionRelay-7199`, `viewRowDeclaredReads-11013`.
  - Result: `Test Files  142 passed (142)`, `Tests  1530 passed (1530)`, exit 0, at `b07e8ae`.
- **Targeted run, declared narrowing:** the two pin files and the five neighbouring data-table suites ran outside the lock with `--maxWorkers=1`, at `80a7e35`: `7 passed (7)`, `41 passed (41)`. The lock was held by the objectui#12030 dev's multi-package runs while this run queued for 3 × 540 s. Every full run above went through the lock.
- **Repo checks, each exit 0 at `b07e8ae`:**
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`
  - `pnpm check:changeset-claims`
  - `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`)
  - `pnpm check:control-bytes`
  - `pnpm check:test-path-roots`
  - `pnpm check:vi-mock-specifiers`
  - `pnpm check:handler-key-reads`
  - also `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-example-ids` and `check:doc-json`.
- **eslint, a proven narrowing:**
  - **Population:** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` read 3 files, which is the diff's whole eslint population. The other three changed files are `.md` / `.mdx`, and no `files:` glob in `eslint.config.js` matches them; the config globs `ts` / `tsx` only.
  - **Result:** `data-table.tsx` reads E1 W39, identical to the same file at `b64fda3`. The one error is the pre-existing `react-hooks/static-components`. The two new test files read E0, with W3 and W4 (`no-explicit-any`, as in the sibling pins).
  - **Why the narrowing holds:** linting is not type-aware (`eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- **NOT MEASURED:** `check:doc-snippets`, `check:doc-examples` and `check:readme-exports`.
  - Reason: each refuses to run without every package's `dist/` (a whole-tree build). The doc and README edits here add no fenced block, so none of the three has anything of this diff to read.
- **CI note:** `Spec Main Shape Gate` is red on `main` and is advisory. Its consumer half is objectui#12325.

## Acceptance notes

- In the console, `ObjectGrid`'s editors are injected widgets that stage on every change, so a value typed there during a save was already staged. It was lost to the settle's rebuild, and the editor was closed under the user. Both are covered by the grid pins and the components pins.
- **Not changed:** an editor that was open before the save, whose value was sent, and that is Escaped during the save. It reverts to its snapshot and may remove the column. The settle then has nothing to remove, and the record holds the sent value, which the re-read draws. Nothing is dropped silently there, but the Escape cannot un-send the value.
- **Cost of the in-flight rule:** if a save fails after a cell was re-edited back to its loaded value, the cell stays pending with a value equal to the record's. That costs one redundant write, and the next commit on that cell un-stages it.
